project.title: Ray Tracer
project.summary: A CPU-based path tracer written in Rust with BVH acceleration, soft shadows, and multi-threading.

sections.title: Overview
sections.body: I built this ray tracer from scratch in Rust to learn about computer graphics and low-level optimization. It supports diffuse and specular materials, soft shadows via area lights, and a bounding volume hierarchy (BVH) for fast intersection culling. Rendering is multi-threaded using Rayon.

sections.title: Architecture
sections.body:
The codebase is split into three crates:

- `core` — vector math, ray primitives, and color math
- `bvh` — bounding volume hierarchy construction and traversal
- `cli` — command-line interface, image output, and scene parsing

Rays are traced recursively with a maximum depth to prevent infinite reflection loops. The BVH reduces the per-pixel intersection cost from O(n) to O(log n) over scene geometry.

sections.title: Planning
sections.body:
Development was split into milestones:
1. Basic ray-sphere intersection and PPM output
2. Material system (Lambertian, metal, dielectric)
3. BVH acceleration structure
4. Multi-threaded rendering and CLI polish

Each milestone was tested with a rendered scene before moving to the next.
